alignments.note: Waw of the consecutive/presentative frame rendered *And* (rule 14).

Presentative הָיָה frame *it shall come to pass ... that* (rules 21, 45). The temporal clause is introduced by כְּ's own *when* (t007), so the frame's complementizer is the *that* at the head of the apodosis (t036), not the first subordinator written; unit discontinuous across the temporal clause under rule 25.
Temporal כְּ before infinitive construct recast as a finite clause takes *when* (rule 52).
Infinitive construct נוּחַ keeps the verb with its supplied auxiliary (rule 52); discontinuous from כְּ under rule 25.
Construct noun with a supplied *the*, since no article morpheme stands on it (rule 29).
Nomen rectum of כַּפּוֹת takes the relational *of* (rule 19); the second *the* is supplied on this inner construct, which carries no article morpheme (rule 29).
Article on כֹּהֲנִים takes the *the* standing before its own word (rule 29, arthrous rendering).
Rectum takes the relational *of* and its own noun (rule 19).
Articleless attributive participle recast as a relative clause keeps the supplied relative with the attributive itself (rule 41).
Construct noun with supplied *the*; its rectum is a bare proper name (rule 29).
Rectum takes the relational *of* (rule 19).
Construct אֲדוֹן with supplied *the*; its rectum כֹּל carries no article (rule 29).
Quantifying construct: the *of* between אֲדוֹן and כֹּל is that chain's relation and belongs to this rectum (rule 19); no second *of* is written before the earth.
Article on אֶרֶץ takes the *the* standing before its own word (rule 15).
Noun.
Locative בְּ → *in* (rule 11).
Construct מֵי with a supplied *the*; the article of the phrase stands on the rectum (rule 29).
Article on the toponym takes the *the* standing before its own word (rule 29).
Rectum takes the relational *of* (rule 19).
Second construct מֵי, read exactly as the first (rules 19, 29).
Article on the toponym takes its own *the* (rule 29).
Rectum takes the relational *of* (rule 19).
Niphal imperfect with its auxiliaries; *off* is the phrasal particle of *cut off* and the head stays on the lexical verb (rules 17, 44).
Paragogic nun has no English realization (rule 32).

Appositional *even* introducing the resumed phrase; no object marker or connective morpheme stands in the verse to license it, so it is added rather than folded into the article or noun beside it (rules 16, 30).
Article → *the* (rule 15).
Noun.
Attributive article on the participle rendered by the relative *that* (rule 41).
Participle with its phrasal particle *down*; head stays on the lexical verb (rule 44).
מִן → *from* (rule 11).
The לְ of מִלְמַעְלָה has no English word of its own: the ASV writes only *from above*, whose two words are taken by מִן and by מַעַל with its directive he (rule 40).
Host and directive he share the single English word written for them, headed on the morpheme carrying the lexeme; rule 32 lists מַעְלָה → *above* as this shape.
Waw → *and* (rule 14).
Finite verb with its subject pronoun and auxiliary (rule 17).
Noun of the adverbial accusative phrase.

Adverbial accusative נֵד אֶחָד: the supplied *in* goes to the word it stands before, which is the numeral opening the English phrase (rule 33), as with `תֹּכֶן אֶחָד` → *of one measure*. The competing reading attaches *in* to נֵד as the phrase's head noun; I took the rule's stated placement.

review_notes: The frame *that* of הָיָה is t036 at the head of the apodosis, not t007, which is כְּ's *when* over the temporal clause (rule 45's counting sentence).
*even* (t046) is left added: the verse writes no object marker and no connective for it.
*in one heap*: the supplied preposition was placed on אֶחָד per rule 33's word-it-stands-before instruction; attaching it to נֵד is the materially plausible alternative.
